newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up, mkt calms on C Bank move.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up, mkt calms on C Bank move.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended slightly up on Monday at 26.367 from 26.37 after the Central Bank's strong intervention in recent days, traders said.
"No one lifted the Central Bank's offer anymore. The market had calmed down," a foreign bank dealer said.
The Central Bank in recent days was forced to unload dollars to inject sobriety in a market that became jittery on talks the Philippines may be the next Thailand.
A property slump in the Thai market had affected banks.
The Central Bank also raised its overnight borrowing rate last Friday to 10.25 percent from 10 to make it more expensive to hold on to dollars.
"The peso's movement was just sideways. There was no significant factor to perk up the rate," a big bank trader said.
The slight rise in Treasury bill rates at the regular auction on Monday had little impact on the peso.
Volume fell to $102.5 million from $198.3 million.
Dealers said the peso is likely to trade sideways from 26.363/26.37 on Tuesday.
